# Mechanic coverage matrix

This is the traceability matrix for the rewrite. Each row is one legacy mechanic. A mechanic counts as ported only when every column is filled and the test exists (architecture.md, "Mechanic coverage").

How it was built:
- The legacy source (`/Users/egedogan_dursun/aerona`, read only) was parsed with acorn. Every top-level function, arrow function, class and constant, every large nested function, every `yield` step of the engine generators, every `tool(...)` definition and every route of `server.js` was extracted (counts in Appendix B).
- The extracted items were split into 19 work packages by file, plus one package (group NEW) for mechanics that decisions.md adds with no legacy counterpart. Each package was read in full against the spec. Inline mechanics that the parser cannot see (blocks between `yield` steps, pipeline steps inside one function, switch branches, table-driven tool definitions) were added by hand.
- Every extracted function-like item is accounted for. It is either named in the Legacy source column of a row, or listed in Appendix A as folded into a row, assigned to the rules registry, treated as catalog data, or not ported (with the reason). A script verified this for every package.

Column conventions:
- **Legacy source**: `file:function`, relative to the legacy repo root. Line ranges mark inline blocks.
- **Spec section**: `NN §x › heading` refers to `docs/spec/NN-*.md` (03-rules-registry.md is not cited; tunables are folded as `RULES:<NS>`). `GAP — …` means no spec file describes the behaviour. All GAPs are listed below.
- **New module**: backend paths are relative to `backend/src/aerona/` and frontend paths to `frontend/src/` (feature folders). `migrations/` means an Alembic migration or a schema constraint.
- **Auto trigger**: when the mechanic runs without the player. "—" means it never runs on its own.
- **Manual control**: the existing control is written as the new endpoint followed by the old one. `needed` means the legacy app had no manual control; architecture rule 6 requires one, and a proposal may follow.
- **Test** and **Status** start as `todo` and `planned`. Implementation agents update them.
- IDs are stable. New rows are appended at the end of their group with the next free number.

### Mechanics required by decisions.md with no spec and no legacy code (13)

These rows (group NEW) come from decisions that introduce new behaviour. The spec does not define them yet, and the legacy code has nothing to port.

| ID | Mechanic | Missing definition |
|---|---|---|
| NEW-001 | Lore output language chosen once in the genesis wizard (English default, Turkish available), stored on the world, immutable, passed to every prompt as an output-language directive | decision 1: no spec section defines the language field, the wizard step or the directive fragment |
| NEW-002 | Output-language directive fragment injected into every prompt template | decision 1: directive fragment not in 09 §1 shared fragments |
| NEW-003 | Son sanity stat: cosmic horror (leak, Outer Beings, forbidden knowledge) erodes it, tunable thresholds trigger effects on the son's turn | decision 47: legacy sons have no sanity stat; 06 §8 covers community and mortal sanity only |
| NEW-004 | Son sanity thresholds change son behaviour (clouded prompts, tool limits, madness acts) | decision 47: effects of low son sanity undefined |
| NEW-005 | Tier-unlock table: each civilization tier unlocks engine actions (beyond mortal tools) and is applied by the engine and goals | decision 48: no spec defines the tier-unlock table |
| NEW-006 | Mechanics for the seven designed world types not in legacy (ringed, asteroid belt, tidally locked, void pocket, god's palace, generation ship, corpse-world): physics, birth rules, travel and engine effects | decision 45: 06 §2 lists only the 11 built types |
| NEW-007 | Declared but unused rules wired into their mechanic: DEATH rite_devotion, rite_cost, kill_refund, and the rite's devotion and prosperity effects | decision 32: 07 §5 lists these keys but no rule reads them |
| NEW-008 | Seeded RNG per engine tick derived from world seed and epoch number; every random draw in engine phases uses it | decision 37: legacy uses Math.random everywhere |
| NEW-009 | No transaction spans an await: each engine phase is its own unit of work under the single writer lock | decision 23 |
| NEW-010 | Creation costs, rarity turn limits, prompt caps, mortal-agent settings and stream timings are rules-registry tunables, not constants | decision 24: these numbers are hard-coded in legacy |
| NEW-011 | Rule groups split by subsystem; every key lives with the subsystem that reads it; unused keys are wired up or removed | decision 55 |
| NEW-012 | One export model renders both the printable HTML book and the Markdown codex | decision 33: 07 §9-10 describe two separate builders |
| NEW-013 | Guest world opens read-only side by side through a separate DB connection; the live database is never swapped | decision 60: 02 §23 describes the legacy swap |

## Open issues for the integrator

The work packages found these conflicts between the spec, the decisions and the legacy code. Each one is attached to the row that carries it. Resolve them in the spec, or confirm the row, before implementing the row.

| Kind | Row | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| Spec text vs decision | MORT-018 | 04 §3 says mortal creations skip Fate; decision 41 reviews them in batch, and 10 §3.8 already feeds mortal records to Fate. Update 04 §3. |
| Spec text vs decision | LLM-080 | 08 §4.6.2 runs judgment and chronicle in parallel; decision 17 runs the chronicler after verdicts are committed. Update 08 §4.6.2. |
| Spec text vs decision | LLM-062 | 08 §4.6.3 lets a reject fall through to accept when Fate is off; decision 18 stores an explicit unjudged verdict. Update 08 §4.6.3. |
| Spec text vs decision | MOOD-006 | Legacy creator worship never closes the entity's other worship bonds; decision 27 (single patron) requires it. |
| Spec text vs decision | GOAL-005 | Goals and achievements count active enemy bonds as wars; decision 35 makes the wars table the only source. |
| Spec text vs decision | INT-019 | Legacy peace miracle only closes enmity bonds; decision 43 also ends ongoing wars through the war-resolution service. |
| Spec text vs decision | SVC-128 | Legacy path finder handles only entity and son nodes (02 §28.5); decision 11 extends it to the Creator, worlds and foreign gods. |
| Spec text vs code | ENG-028 | 04 §1 Phase 4 places resource regeneration in the epoch transition; the code runs it in the tick. The row follows the code. |
| Spec text vs code | CORE-047 | 02 §9 says son relations are rounded on change; the code only clamps. The row follows the code. |
| Conflicting legacy behaviours | INV-003 | Shared throne: the legacy repair keeps the oldest ruler, the bond write path keeps the newest. The bond service must pick one. |
| Text matching to replace (decision 16) | INV-046 | Shared-theme detection (ORTAK_TEMA regex) needs a structured flag in Fate's network-repair output; no spec defines it. |
| Text matching to replace (decision 16) | INV-050 | Denial detection (INKAR regex) needs a structured verdict field from Fate; no spec defines it. |
| Text matching to replace (decision 16) | INV-037 | Died-in-event detection (OLUM_SOZU regex) needs a structured death cause on the record. |
| Text matching to replace (decision 16) | CTX-029 | Son memory 'events about you' and thread advancement use LIKE matching on chronicle text; switch to structured chronicle-son links and thread tags. |
| Text matching to replace (decision 59) | CORE-054 | Tired-motif rows describe the legacy text-frequency algorithm; the rewrite counts Fate's motif tags. Only thresholds, canon exemption and per-world logic carry over. |
| Text matching to replace (decision 28) | REP-002 | Legacy reads passions and reputation events by grepping chronicle text; the action-kind to passion table (catalog/passions.py) must be built. |
| Explicit fields (decision 40) | POW-014 | The angry curse pool finds temples by name substrings; needs a typed temple field. |
| Decaying window (decision 31) | MOOD-012 | Legacy counts unanswered prayers all-time; the row uses a decaying window with tunable length and decay. |
| Registry coverage (decision 24) | DATA-015 | Starting gameplay values live as schema defaults (son existence 60, world danger 20, ...); move them into the rules registry. |
| Endpoint naming | API-007 | GET /api/iliskiler is proposed as GET /api/sons/relations here and GET /api/relations in UI-170. Pick one. |
| Dropped endpoint kept for traceability | API-094 | POST /api/ek (Turkish suffix override) keeps a row so every route is traced; it is not ported (decisions 14, 44). |

## Cross-package overlaps

These row pairs come from different work packages, name the same legacy function (with overlapping or unspecified line ranges) and sit in different modules. Pairs where one row is the LLM prompt role and the other the orchestration or effects of the same call are intentional and not listed. Usually one row describes the shared rule and the other its wrapper (ledger, cost, endpoint semantics). Before implementation, confirm the split and make sure the rule itself is implemented once, in the first module, and only called from the second.

The scan found no such pair outside the LLM role rows.

### Player actions with a wrapper row and a rule row

For these legacy endpoints, two packages each wrote an ACT row: one for the `epoch.js` wrapper (ledger, cost, refund, busy lock, events) and one for the rule in the owning legacy module. The rows usually sit in the same module, so one agent implements them together. Treat each set as one endpoint handler: the wrapper row supplies the transaction and ledger semantics and the rule rows supply the effects.
